## Telework Related Questions

### 2025 New Work From Home Question (`work_from_home`)

**Does each person ever work from home?**

- No
- Yes, some of the time (less than 50% of the time)
- Yes, most of the time (at least 50% but less than 100% of the time)
- Yes, all of the time (100% of the time)

:::{.callout-note}
#### Logic

- *if household has 1 or more members who worked for pay/profit or were on leave last week*
- *if household has 1 member or more ‘on leave': For any household member on leave (e.g., parental leave, medical leave), please respond based on their work arrangements prior to leave.*
- Programmer: Show list of persons age 16+ with paid_work = “yes” or “on leave”

:::
   
### Telework Frequency (`telecommute_freq`)

**Currently, how many days <do you/does name> typically work from home or telework (instead of going to work that day)?**

- 6-7 days a week
- 5 days a week
- 4 days a week
- 3 days a week
- 2 days a week
- 1 day a week
- 1-3 days a month
- Less than monthly
- Never *hide if job_type is work ONLY from home or remotely (telework, self-employed)*

:::{.callout-note}
#### Logic

- Programmer: if (paid_work is “yes” or “on leave”) AND work_from_home is NOT “all of the time”

:::

## Teleworker and Telework Status Definitions

:::{.callout-important}
Data universe for this analysis: full/part time or self-employed workers
:::

The following analysis has two ways of identifying teleworkers and telework status:

1. **Teleworkers** are the workers who telecommute more than one day per week or work fully at home
2. **Telework status** assignments
   - [Fully At Home]{style="color:#91268F"}: workers working from home all of the time
   - [Hybrid]{style="color:#00A7A0"}: workers working from home some or most (not all) of the time and telecommuting at least 1 day/week
   - [Fully In Person]{style="color:#8CC63E"}: workers telecommuting less than 1 day/week

## Telework Trend

- Roughly two-thirds of workers worked [fully in person]{style="color:#91268F"} outside of home in 2023 and 2025.
- Those who work [fully at home]{style="color:#91268F"} peaked in 2021 at about one-third.
- [Hybrid workers]{style="color:#00A7A0"} made up about one-quarter of all workers from 2021 to 2025.

## Commute Mode Share

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
Sample sizes were low for commuting with other modes in 2021
:::

- Most workers who travel outside of home for work drove.
- Workers who took transit decreased significantly in 2021 and stayed around 7\% to 9\% (differences are within margins of error) since.
- Active Modes (incl. walk, bike and micromobility) is consistently at 4\% to 6\% (differences are within margins of error)

## Telework by demographic characteristics

### Household income

- Strong positive correlation between income and working from home
- The share of teleworkers for households with income under $50,000 were not affected by the pandemic
- The share of teleworkers for households earning \$50,000 or more increased significantly in 2021 during the pandemic. Since the pandemic, The share for households earning \$50,000 to \$99,999 dropped to almost pre-pandemic levels while the share for households earning \$100,000 or more are still more than 40\%.
